subject: Nimble failing to index into vector of booleans when nested in if statement

messages.author: 566bb36c21759db8
messages.subject: Nimble failing to index into vector of booleans when nested in if statement
parts:
Hi all, 



I have a vector of booleans and I am trying to access the elements in an if statement that is nested within a for loop ie:


for(i in 1:10){
  if(bool_vec[i]){
    do task . . .
  }else{
    don't do task
  }
}

If I access the elements of the boolean vector explicitly (ie bool_vec[1], bool_vec[2], etc.) then I have no issues, but if I try and index with i I get the following error while building my model:

Error in eval(code[[2]], constantsEnv) : object 'i' not found

Does anybody see something I might be doing wrong, or know if this is just an issue in nimble that hasn't been fixed yet?



(Here is a link to stack overflow where I initially asked the question: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/50764920/nimble-failing-to-index-into-vector-of-booleans-when-nested-in-if-statement )


Best, 

Felix

messages.subject: Re: Nimble failing to index into vector of booleans when nested in if statement
parts:
Hi Felix,

Can you send a more complete example?

From the stack overflow question, it sounds like this is in model code.  If so, it won't work because model code is declarative.  Each line declares a node in a graphical model.  For loops declare groups of nodes.  The way the example is shown looks like imperative (i.e. typical) programming.  Code in nimbleFunctions uses imperative programming.  If you can explain what you want to set up, we can try to help you work it out.

Perry

          meanAIS[i + indOffset[j]]<- muP[j]*mumIS[i + indOffset[j]]/MIS_[j]/k[i + indOffset[j]]

          meanAPC[i + indOffset[j]]<- pPC[i + indOffset[j]]*mumPC[i + indOffset[j]]/MPC_/k[i + indOffset[j]]
          APC[i + indOffset[j]]~T(dnorm(meanAPC[i + indOffset[j]],uAPC[i + indOffset[j]]),0,)
         
        }
      }
     
     
    })


Above I have highlighted the code that I want to included in yellow. Essentially I want to change the prior for each muP[j] based on some external information that will change with each run. 

Thank you so much for your quick response, and please let me know if there is anything that I can clear up. 

Aside:  I have noticed that the compile time is a little slow, do you have any recommendations on how I could decrease the time it takes to compile?

Best, 
Felix

messages.subject: Re: Nimble failing to index into vector of booleans when nested in if statement
parts:
Hi Felix,

That's an interesting case.  Thanks.  I want to think about that kind of flexibility in the future.  For now, here is a solution (set up with toy distributions) that does what I think you want:

mc <- nimbleCode({
    for(i in 1:3) {
        x[INDS[i]] ~ dunif(0,1)
    }
    for(i in 1:2) {
        x[INDS2[i]] ~ dunif(-1, 0)
    }
})

INDS <- c(1, 3, 5) ## indices where bool_vec is TRUE
INDS2 <- c(2, 4)   ## indices where bool_vec is FALSE
m <- nimbleModel(mc, constants = list(INDS = INDS, INDS2 = INDS2))

Improving compile time is one of our long-term development goals.  Unfortunately I can't give any great tricks.  You can speed up nimbleModel by using calculate = FALSE, check = FALSE.  You can speed up configureMCMC by using useConjugacy = FALSE if you do not actually need any Gibbs samplers.  But there's not much we can do for the compiler until we manage some real development advances.

Perry
